title: Inlet Orchestra: weight hydration, conversion, and performance gating for OSS LLMs
creator: Aisha Mendes
description: Create an automated end-to-end intake workflow (Inlet Orchestra) that hydrates incoming community weights, performs deterministic conversion to Redwood runtime artifacts, runs multi-stage validation (binary checks, functional smoke, and perf profiling), and publishes a pinned model artifact + performance profile to the catalog. The flow must be resilient to partial failures, surface clear remediation steps, and produce telemetry for capacity planning.
background: We onboard increasing numbers of open-source LLMs with varied source formats (PyTorch .bin, safetensors, HF sharded checkpoints, Flax). Current ad-hoc handoffs cause slow turnarounds and inconsistent runtime quality. The onboarding team needs a repeatable pipeline that standardizes conversion outputs, enforces performance gates (latency/throughput/peak memory), and creates a single canonical pin that the serving runtime and Console can consume.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Given a new OSS LLM tarball, pipeline completes deterministic conversion to Redwood artifact format and publishes a pin if all gates pass.
2) Binary integrity checks (checksums, manifest schema) run and fail fast on mismatch.
3) Functional smoke tests (generation quality on 8 curated prompts) pass threshold or report regression metrics.
4) Performance profile (99th latency, avg token/sec, peak GPU memory) is produced and stored in catalog.
5) If any gate fails, pipeline creates a triage ticket with logs, diffs vs baseline, and marks artifact as quarantined.
6) Telemetry emitted for conversion time, failure reason, and resource usage.
7) Documentation and runbook updated with recovery steps.
implementation_notes:
- Input formats supported initially: safetensors, PyTorch single-file, HF sharded, Flax.
- Conversion path: normalize weights -> strip training-only state -> reserialize into Redwood runtime bundle (.rwb) with embedded manifest and checksums.
- Use containerized conversion worker with CPU-bound pre-processing and GPU smoke runner for perf checks.
- Perf profiling uses standardized 32-token/512-token workloads on an n1-gpu-small test harness to compute latency distribution and KV-cache behavior.
- Quality smoke uses deterministic temperature/seed and compares token-level top-k similarity against a reference baseline where available.
- Pin naming: catalog pin = model_family@version+redwood-variant (e.g., llama2-13b@v0.1+rwq8).
- All artifacts go through content-addressed storage and signed manifests.
tasks:
- Create conversion worker Docker image and CI pipeline (Aisha)
- Implement manifest validator and checksum verifier (Lena)
- Design quality smoke harness and prompt set, add golden baselines where available (MLR)
- Implement perf profiling harness and resource accounting (Infra)
- Integrate with catalog publish API and pin issuance (Platform)
- Add telemetry events and Grafana dashboards for onboarding metrics (Observability)
- Author runbook and postmortem template for quarantined artifacts (SRE)
- End-to-end integration tests and canary sign-off (QA)
progress_updates:
2026-03-03: Kickoff meeting with Platform, Infra, and Observability; agreed on target perf metrics and artifact format.
2026-03-06: Prototype conversion container built; supports safetensors and single-file PyTorch. Early checksum validator implemented.
2026-03-09: Quality smoke harness scaffolded with 12 prompts; initial pass shows differences for a community-contributed variant due to tokenization mismatch. Added tokenization normalization step.
2026-03-12: Perf harness runs on n1-gpu-small; discovered a memory spike for 32k context during KV warmup — gating thresholds adjusted and an alert created (ENG-513321).
2026-03-14: Integration with catalog publish API stubbed; created first end-to-end dry run that reaches the publish stage but blocked by missing signature key rotation (security).
risks:
- Upstream weight formats can include training-specific tensors (optimizer state) or unexpected dtype that breaks conversion; mitigation: strict manifest checks and fast quarantine.
- Quality regressions: our smoke set is limited and may miss user-critical failure modes; mitigation: expand prompt coverage and run optional decode-evals before final pin.
- Resource costs: perf profiling on many models can consume substantial GPU time; mitigation: triage models by manifest metadata and sample for full profiling only.
- Signing/keys: publish blocked if key rotation or KMS outage — require fallback signing policy or human override.
rollout_plan:
1) Feature-flag pipeline in staging and run continuous dry-runs against a curated queue of 10 community models.
2) Open invite to select model contributors for closed beta.
3) After two weeks of stable dry-runs and no critical regressions, enable automated pins for low-risk families (based on size and manifest quality).
4) Gradually increase to full automation with manual review band for high-impact models (>=70B).
5) Post-launch: monitor onboarding success rate and conversion latency; target 95% success on first attempt.
qa_plan:
- Unit tests for conversion steps and manifest validator.
- Integration tests: feed known good/bad tarballs and assert expected quarantine/publish outcomes.
- Regression tests: compare smoke outputs against golden baselines and assert similarity thresholds.
- Load test: run 50 concurrent conversion jobs in CI-proxy to validate queue and worker autoscaling.
- Manual canary: onboard a low-risk 7B community model and verify serving runtime in a dedicated environment.
notes: Decisions to record: use safetensors-first policy for ingestion to favor deterministic deserialization; allow PyTorch fallback when safetensors absent. We will not perform full quantized conversion automatically for night-0 pin — quantized variants will be suggested by Optimize pipeline after initial publish. Follow-up: add CI gating to prevent publishing of artifacts missing provenance fields (author, upstream-hash, license).
